AfterDamageReceived.rationale: All five C# clauses (DemonTongue.cs:21) map one-for-one onto demon_tongue.py:34-39, and the two that could have gone wrong are verdicted on their own guards. `CombatState != null` is structural (the hook is only dispatched by a live CombatState); `CombatState.CurrentSide == Owner.Creature.Side` is `self.combat.current_side == 'player'`; `target == Owner.Creature` is `target is self.player`; `result.UnblockedDamage > 0` is `amount > 0` (guard G2); `!_triggeredThisTurn` is `not self._triggered_this_turn`, latched before the heal exactly as C# latches before CreatureCmd.Heal. Executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py demon-tongue): 7 unblockable self-damage on the player's turn leaves HP at 60 of 60 (fully healed) and a second 5 on the same turn leaves 55 (not healed).

BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: C#'s hook is audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 9, before the block clear; the sim's on_player_turn_start is executed-confirmed to sit after the block clear and the energy reset (py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order prints on_block_cleared -> on_energy_reset -> on_player_turn_start). Only a flag RESET happens here, and nothing in the intervening window can observe it: a scan of every ported on_block_cleared and on_energy_reset implementation -- relics/anchor.py:21, captains_wheel.py:19, fake_anchor.py:24, horn_cleat.py:19, art_of_war.py:37, venerable_tea_set.py:27, fake_venerable_tea_set.py:29 and powers.py:1625 / :3445 / :4781 / :4983 (re-verified 2026-08-04, was :1214 / :2766 / :3841 / :4032 -- all four still grant Block via BlockCmd.apply or Energy via EnergyCmd.gain) -- shows every one of them grants Block or Energy and not one deals damage to the player, which is the only way to read _triggered_this_turn. Same reasoning and same verdict as audit/records/relic/brilliant_scarf.json's BeforeSideTurnStart entry and relic/beating_remnant's in batch 1 (binding rule 3): recorded as a divergence rather than faithful because the slot genuinely differs and a future damage-to-player effect placed on AfterBlockCleared or AfterEnergyReset would expose it. `participants.Contains(Owner.Creature)` (DemonTongue.cs:31-34) is structurally satisfied -- on_player_turn_start is dispatched only for the player side. Rule 7: powers.py is hashed by this record (extra_sources); the scanned sibling relic files (anchor, art_of_war, captains_wheel, fake_anchor, fake_venerable_tea_set, horn_cleat, venerable_tea_set) are also hashed by this record (extra_sources).

guards.what: G1: the killing-blow guard (PROMPT.md bug class 2) -- C# skips the victim's AfterDamageReceived when the blow killed it (CreatureCmd.cs:390-393 `!WasTargetKilled || !IsDead`)
guards.rationale: Confirmed rather than assumed, because Demon Tongue is a HEAL on the player and an unguarded version would resurrect the Ironclad from a lethal Offering. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04 against a real behavior change since this was last audited: the preventer path no longer floors a prevented death's HP to 1 (cmds.py:538's docstring: 'now that the corpse is left at 0' -- CreatureCmd.cs:565 -- so a preventer like Lizard Tail heals explicitly from its own `after_preventing_death`, cmds.py's dead-creature heal guard was dropped accordingly). This does NOT reopen the guard: `was_lethal = target.is_dead` (cmds.py:398/407) is a SNAPSHOT taken immediately after the HP write and BEFORE `_resolve_death` runs (cmds.py:402), mirroring `Creature.LoseHpInternal`'s `WasTargetKilled` plus the `IsDead` read `CreatureCmd.cs:392` makes -- both happen strictly BEFORE `Kill()` in C# too (CreatureCmd.cs:409), so a prevented-and-healed death can never un-skip the dispatch on EITHER side; the dispatch is gated on `if not was_lethal:` at cmds.py:444 (was :121-122, `if not target.is_dead:`), unconditionally on the pre-resolution snapshot. Same mechanism and same verdict as relic/beating_remnant's AfterDamageReceived entry in batch 1 (binding rule 3).

guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# heals `result.UnblockedDamage`, which EXCLUDES OverkillDamage; the sim heals the raw `hp_lost`, which includes it
guards.issue: MECHANISM: DamageResult.cs documents UnblockedDamage as the damage the target received after blocking and OverkillDamage as the excess past 0 HP, and they are separate fields (CreatureCmd.cs:294 has to ADD them back together when it wants the total). The sim's DamageCmd passes `hp_lost` (cmds.py:445, was :122), which is the full post-block, post-ModifyHpLost amount and is never clamped to the victim's current HP -- `target.hp = max(0, target.hp - hp_lost)` clamps the HP, not the number. So a lethal-but-prevented hit heals MORE in the sim than in C#. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, and the concrete unported thing is named): the two amounts can only differ when overkill exists, i.e. on a blow that takes the player to 0, and the killing-blow guard of G1 suppresses the hook entirely unless something PREVENTS the death. The sim's only ported should_die preventers are relics/lizard_tail.py:35, potions.py:1394-1395 (Fairy in a Bottle -- IS ported/in-scope, corrected 2026-08-04: the prior 'out of scope' phrasing pre-dates the shared contract's 2026-07-26 potion ruling and was never a waiver verdict on this record, but the wording was wrong and is fixed here; Fairy in a Bottle's own heal is a SEPARATE mechanism from Demon Tongue's, so this correction does not change G2's dormancy) and three enemy powers (powers.py:1566, :2016, :3365) that protect enemies, not the player -- and Lizard Tail's own C# body heals the player to a fraction of max HP, which the Heal then cannot exceed. Porting a player-side death preventer that leaves the player at 0-1 HP makes it live, as does any effect that heals more than max HP. Filed as a gap rather than waived because 'no ported content reaches the difference' is today's content, not the divergence's shape (binding rule 1). Rule 7: cmds.py, potions.py, powers.py, relics/lizard_tail.py and CreatureCmd.cs are hashed by this record (extra_sources); DamageResult.cs is not.

guards.what: G3: `_triggeredThisTurn` is reset at a TURN boundary and at no combat boundary -- on EITHER side (PROMPT.md bug class 13)
guards.rationale: The pool-wide scan (.superpowers/sdd/content-relic-sweeps.md sweep A) puts this relic in the 'reset only at a turn boundary' bucket, which that document explicitly does NOT clear -- it requires a trace to the first READER of the stale field. Two facts settle it. (a) SYMMETRY: DemonTongue.cs has no AfterCombatEnd / AfterCombatVictory / BeforeCombatStart override at all, so C# carries the flag across combats exactly as the sim does; unlike relic/belt_buckle there is no C# reset the port dropped. (b) SHADOWING, executed (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b04.py demon-tongue): a relic instance left at _triggered_this_turn=True by combat 1 reads False as soon as combat 2 is constructed, because CombatState.__init__ runs the first player turn and demon_tongue.py:44-45 clears it -- so no reader ever sees the stale value. This is the relic/art_of_war shape, not the relic/belt_buckle shape.

cmds.py:532-, was :157-166, caps the heal at max HP and fires on_hp_changed -- RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-04: the dead-target no-op guard described here has since been REMOVED from CreatureCmd.heal (a real, unrelated fix -- 'now that the corpse is left at 0, that guard would block the very revives it exists for'); this relic's own heal is never reached with a dead target anyway (G1's guard already skips the whole hook on a killing blow), so the removal does not change Demon Tongue's own verdict -- the same three properties as CreatureCmd.Heal. The relic passes no applier and no card source on either side, so it creates no new interaction with relic/unsettling_lamp's applier-gated doubling (the same check relic/belt_buckle's N3 makes for the same reason). RULE 7: cmds.py is not hashed here.
